title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
desc: Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through a fusion engine provide a flexible pathway for prognostic risk ranking from sleep recordings, while reliable CVD screening will require independent external cohorts and explicit confounder control.

title: Unimodal imaging foundation models and vision-language models in MRI: A systematic review of emerging methods and clinical applications.
desc: [Cell reports. Medicine] Artificial intelligence in medical imaging is shifting from task-specific algorithms toward adaptable foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). However, applying these models to MRI remains challenging because clinical interpretation requires integrating multi-parametric, volumetric imaging across multiple sequences with clinical context. This systematic review evaluates 35 studies on unimodal FMs and multimodal VLMs in MRI, summarizing emerging architectures, downstream applications, and challenges to clinical translation. Current research is concentrated in neuroimaging, with diagnostic classification representing the most mature application. Segmentation and outcome prediction also show promise, whereas automated report generation remains limited by poor clinical fidelity despite strong linguistic fluency. Broader adoption is hindered by heterogeneous MRI acquisition, limited large-scale paired image-text datasets, and inadequate safety-focused evaluation metrics. Advancing clinical translation will require standardized multicenter datasets, stronger integration with electronic health records and pathology, robust evaluation frameworks, and improved model explainability.

title: Deep learning-based detection and classification of airway nodules on CT for early medical intervention.
desc: [Insights into imaging] Airway lesions are common CT findings in interval and post-screen lung cancers; however, airway nodules are frequently overlooked. Robust artificial intelligence (AI) tools for characterizing airway nodules remain limited. This study aimed to develop and evaluate deep learning-based models for the detection and classification of airway nodules on low-dose CT(LDCT) as a second-reading tool. 1813 segmental and more proximal airway nodules were retrospectively identified from 1107 LDCT of 1043 participants. A sphere-based center-points matching network, first used to establish a lung nodule detection model, was transferred to airway nodules and enhanced by incorporating coordinate and multiscale attention. The model was trained on 907 proximal airway nodules and independently tested on 738 proximal nodules across four hospitals. The clinical utility of the AI tool was evaluated through human-AI interaction. For nodule classification, a 3D SEResNeXt101-based model was trained, validated and tested using 286 airway nodules (121 benign, 165 malignant) with a 6:2:2 split and evaluated in an independent testing dataset. On the independent testing set, the detection model achieved a high sensitivity of 73.7%. Human-AI interaction demonstrated AI assistance significantly improved radiologists' performance, increasing sensitivity from 39.5% to 72.9% and F1-score from 49.4% to 77.2%, while reducing diagnosis time from 83.8 s to 61.8 s. The classification model showed high sensitivities of 82.1%, 71.4%, 94.3%, 72.7% and specificities of 62.7%, 73.9%, 73.9%, 87.5% across multicenter training, validation, testing and independent testing sets, respectively. This AI system significantly enhances the detection and classification of proximal airway nodules, guiding early medical intervention. Question Improved early detection and classification of airway nodules are critical for lung cancer mortality reduction, but AI-based CAD systems targeting airway nodules remain scarce. Findings The DL models for detection and classification of proximal airway nodules on chest CT were developed and assisted radiologists to achieve higher detection accuracy. Critical Relevance Statement The clinical applications of the proposed DL-based system for detecting and classifying proximal airway nodules on chest CT scans help radiologists reduce missed/delayed diagnoses and shorten diagnostic time as a second-reading tool, guiding medical intervention and improving clinical outcomes.

Artificial intelligence-driven precision immunogenetics for cancer stem cell-targeted CAR immunotherapy.
source: PubMed · Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute
desc: [Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute] Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are a major contributor to therapeutic resistance, tumour recurrence, and disease progression because of their self-renewal capacity, phenotypic plasticity, immune evasion, and ability to persist after treatment. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based immunotherapy has transformed the treatment of several hematological malignancies, but effective targeting of CSC-driven disease, especially solid tumour, remains challenging. Antigen heterogeneity and loss, CSC plasticity, CAR-cell dysfunction, metabolic constraints, and an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME) can limit long-term therapeutic responses. CSC-associated antigens such as CD133, CD44, EpCAM, HER2, CSPG4, ALDH, and EGFRvIII have been investigated as CAR targets, although their heterogeneous and context-dependent expression raises important concerns regarding CSC specificity and on-target/off-tumour toxicity. Artificial intelligence (AI) and computational approaches provide opportunities to integrate genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, spatial, and clinical data for CSC-associated antigen discovery, biomarker identification, CAR design, patient stratification, and toxicity prediction. However, the evidence supporting these applications varies considerably, ranging from computational and preclinical studies to retrospective clinical modelling, while prospective clinical validation of AI-guided CSC-targeted CAR therapy remains limited. Similarly, next-generation platforms, including CAR-natural killer (CAR-NK) cells, CAR-macrophages (CAR-M), gamma-delta CAR-T cells, and CAR-invariant natural killer T (CAR-iNKT) cells, remain at different stages of translational development. This review critically examines CSC biology, mechanisms of resistance to CAR-based therapy, emerging CAR platforms, and the potential role of AI in precision immunogenetics. Particular emphasis is placed on differentiating CSC-intrinsic, CAR-cell-intrinsic, and TME-mediated resistance and on defining the evidence maturity of AI applications. Finally, current challenges in data availability, tumour heterogeneity, model bias, external validation, interpretability, safety, and prospective clinical translation are discussed, together with priorities for developing clinically validated AI-enabled CSC-targeted CAR therapies.

AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization for childhood brain tumors.
desc: [Nature genetics] Accurate prediction of patient outcomes remains a critical challenge in oncology, in particular for childhood brain tumors, in which treatment decisions need to carefully balance risk of tumor recurrence and death against severe therapy-induced sequelae. Here, we developed MANTIS (methylation profiling and artificial neural networks for time-dependent individualized survival predictions), a precision artificial intelligence (AI) tool for medulloblastoma and ependymoma outcome prediction built on genome-wide DNA methylation array data from 2,786 patients. MANTIS generates individualized survival probabilities over a 10-year period and achieves concordance indices as high as 0.80 ± 0.07, significantly exceeding the predictive accuracy of current clinical indicators. Extending MANTIS to estimate individualized treatment effects identifies ~60% of patients with average-risk medulloblastoma without a significant survival disadvantage (P = 0.683) when treated with less intensive craniospinal irradiation doses, which is associated with improved neurocognitive outcomes. In conclusion, our study establishes a foundation for AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization in childhood brain tumors and offers a blueprint for similar initiatives in other cancer types.

Piloting New Medications for Borderline Personality Disorder: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Psychopharmacological Research.
desc: [Psychopharmacology bulletin] Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) lacks approved pharmacological treatments despite a high symptom burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers new opportunities to accelerate drug discovery and model therapeutic effects. This study will outline an AI-enabled framework for identifying and modelling a novel pharmacological agent for BPD, designed to meet five therapeutic goals: (1) reduce depression without increasing impulsivity and suicidality, (2) reduce suicidality without sedation, (3) limit side effects and weight gain, (4) reduce polypharmacy, and (5) provide combined antidepressant, anti-suicidal, mood-stabilising, and antipsychotic effects. Three AI-driven approaches will be piloted: (1) deep-learning-based compound generation, (2) natural-language-processing (NLP) evidence synthesis, and (3) predictive modelling of symptom trajectories. These methods will be used to design and characterise a hypothetical multimodal compound, BPD-AI-01, including its predicted 3D molecular structure and receptor binding profile. All analyses will use publicly available data and in silico simulations. AI-guided modelling will generate BPD-AI-01, a candidate molecule predicted to act as a partial agonist at 5-HT1A receptors, a modulator at NMDA-associated sites, and a weak antagonist at 5-HT2A/D2 receptors, with low affinity for histaminergic and muscarinic receptors. Its 3D structure will be optimised to balance CNS penetration with reduced metabolic burden. Simulated trajectories will suggest potential antidepressant, anti-suicidal, mood-stabilising, and antipsychotic-like effects without marked sedation or weight gain. AI-enabled pharmacological research may support the design of next-generation medications for BPD that address multiple symptom domains within a single molecule. Empirical validation will be required before any clinical application.

Application of topological deep learning in staging liver fibrosis based on hepatobiliary phase MR images.
desc: [Abdominal radiology (New York)] Early-stage liver fibrosis is reversible; thus, accurate staging of liver fibrosis is of great importance.. Liver biopsy is the gold standard for the diagnosis of liver fibrosis; however, its invasive nature limits its clinical application. Accurate noninvasive staging of liver fibrosis remains challenging. Thus, there is an urgent need for a precise and reliable noninvasive diagnostic approach. A topological deep learning model combining topological data analysis and EfficientViT framework (TopoEfficientViT) was developed to effectively capture global contextual relationships in hepatobiliary phase MR images for assessment of staging liver fibrosis. Our retrospective study included patients with chronic liver diseases from June 2018 to July 2025, which was approved by our Institutional Review Board. Our data from a hospital site (Site A) in our institution were divided into a training set (n = 275) and a validation set (n = 75). The test set (n=65) was composed of data from a separate hospital site (Site B) in the same institution. A total of 415 patients (323 males, mean age 56.52±9.54 years; 92 females, mean age 58.86±9.68 years) were enrolled in the study. In the training set, the AUC and accuracy of TopoEfficientViT for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.942 and 0.906, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.957 and 0.891, respectively. In the validation set, the AUC and accuracy for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.849 and 0.76, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.861and 0.813, respectively. In the test set, the AUC and accuracy for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.829 and 0.769, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.791 and 0.785, respectively. The TopoEfficientViT model had high predictive performance for staging liver fibrosis by integrating multi-scale persistent homology topology with convolutional networks.

Performance of intraoperative artificial intelligence-assisted label-free stimulated Raman histology in recurrent brain tumors.
desc: [Neuro-oncology advances] Therapy-induced tissue alterations complicate intraoperative diagnosis of recurrent central nervous system (CNS) tumors. We evaluated stimulated Raman histology (SRH) combined with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for rapid tumor detection and classification. In this bicentric observational study, fresh tissue from patients undergoing resection or stereotactic biopsy for suspected recurrent CNS tumors was imaged with fiber-laser-based SRH. CNN1 performed binary tumor/non-tumor prediction and CNN2 histotype classification. CNN1 was evaluated against blinded neuropathologist SRH consensus and CNN2 against the final integrated histopathological diagnosis. Of 382 acquired SRH images, 262 images from 143 patients were included. CNN1 achieved an AUC of 0.975 (95% CI, 0.95-1.00) for tumor detection. An exploratory cohort-derived tumor probability threshold of ≥59 increased specificity from 70.7% to 92.0% while maintaining 95.2% sensitivity and identifying 71.4% of radiation necrosis samples. Among 212 images in treatment subgroup analysis, CNN1 accuracy did not differ significantly across prior-treatment groups (overall 90.1%; P = .080). CNN2 accuracy declined from 61.8% after surgery alone to 39.0% after surgery, radiotherapy, and medical treatment (χ2 = 6.04, P = .049). Multimodal therapy was independently associated with lower odds of correct CNN2 prediction (adjusted OR, 0.10 [95% CI, 0.02-0.39]; P = .001 and 0.04 [95% CI, 0.01-0.20]; P < .001). 120/382 images (31.4%) were of insufficient diagnostic quality; application of the quality control threshold would have rejected 84/120 (70.0%). CNN1 maintained high tumor/non-tumor discrimination across treatment subgroups when image quality was sufficient, whereas CNN2 entity-classification performance declined with increasing treatment intensity. Reliable SRH-based diagnosis in recurrent tumors requires validated image-quality control measures and model adaptation to recurrent disease.

Early diagnosis program for multimodal primary open-angle glaucoma based on clinical process.
desc: [Frontiers in ophthalmology] Glaucoma is among the leading causes of blindness. It is important to detect glaucoma at early stages. Using structural and functional examinations to identify primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is critical. Computer-aided diagnosis of glaucoma requires multimodal data to identify an accurate and explainable model for early glaucoma diagnosis. In this study, 301 multimodal data points were collected from the ophthalmology department at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University. Data regarding fundus photography (FP), retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (RNFLt), intraocular pressure (IOP) values, visual field examination parameters and age were obtained. A powerful deep learning network was used to segment the optic nerve head obtained from the FPs. Machine learning classifiers (MLCs) were adopted to obtain the final classification results using 3 datasets: early glaucoma eyes, suspected glaucoma eyes, and healthy eyes; moreover, the diagnostic results of glaucoma specialists and general nonglaucoma ophthalmologists were collected. The overall area under the curve was 0.9858. The accuracy values of the deep learning- machine learning system, the glaucoma specialist group, the general ophthalmologist group were 0.9478, 0.9493, 0.8725, respectively. The algorithm delivers superior results in the early diagnosis of POAG. This study's hybrid deep learning-machine learning framework can effectively assist with clinical decision-making for early POAG.

A Systematic Review of Bias, Validation, and Explainability in Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Dental Diagnostics.
desc: [Journal of dentistry] To critically evaluate the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental diagnosis across multiple dental disciplines, assessing diagnostic performance, methodological quality, risk of bias, validation, explainability, and clinical applicability. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025639340). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, LILACS, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to December-2025. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Risk of bias in diagnostic accuracy studies was assessed using QUADAS-2-tool, evaluating the domains of patient selection, index test, reference standard, flow and timing whilst randomised studies were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2-tool. Reporting quality and transparency of AI-model development and validation were assessed using the selected items from TRIPOD-AI reporting guideline. Methodological quality and risk of bias in AI model development and evaluation were additionally assessed using PROBAST+AI. Ninety-six studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 90.6% were retrospective. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) were the most frequently used architecture (82.3%). Sixteen studies failed to specify the CNN architecture used. Reported diagnostic accuracy ranged from 81% to 99% across dental specialties, with high performance in implantology (92-99%), orthodontics (88-99%), endodontics (87-99%). Panoramic radiographs and cone-beam computed tomography were the most used imaging modalities. QUADAS-2 analysis indicated that high-risk of bias in 55.2% of studies and most lacked external validation, whilst Assessment using selected TRIPOD+AI items identified important gaps in reporting completeness and transparency, particularly in sample-size justification, missing-data handling, protocol availability, study registration, and data or code availability. AI demonstrates substantial technical capability to enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. However, the predominance of retrospective designs, limited external validation, and methodological weaknesses constrain the strength of current evidence. The use of AI is potentially considered as a decision-support tool rather than replacement for clinical judgement.

title: Antibody-drug conjugates: unpacking toxicity profiles and optimized designs for enhanced safety and antitumor efficacy.
source: PubMed · Signal transduction and targeted therapy
desc: [Signal transduction and targeted therapy] Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded treatment options across multiple malignancies, but their clinical benefit remains constrained by heterogeneous and sometimes serious toxicities. These toxicities rarely arise from a single component; instead, they reflect the association between target biology, molecular architecture, systemic exposure, and tissue susceptibility. We first examine the structural basis of ADC toxicity by discussing the distinct contributions of the antibody-target axis, linker, payload, drug loading, and conjugation strategy to systemic exposure and tissue toxicity. We distinguish organ-selective "on-target, off-tumor" injury from target-independent toxicity and further characterize two major off-target routes: context-dependent uptake of intact ADCs through Fcγ receptor-mediated or pinocytosis-dominant pathways, and spatially distinct exposure to released payload arising from premature systemic release or localized bystander diffusion. Furthermore, we summarize a multidisciplinary management framework, ranging from prophylactic measures to graded interventions across complex scenarios such as treatment rechallenge and combination therapy. Finally, we discuss strategies to widen the therapeutic window through exposure-response-guided dosing, next-generation molecular engineering, and emerging conjugate platforms. Artificial intelligence and computational approaches may further extend safety optimization from drug design to patient stratification and real-world surveillance. By linking molecular design, spatial exposure, and clinical management, this review provides an integrated framework to improve ADC safety while preserving antitumor efficacy.

title: Ethical dimensions of artificial intelligence in nursing and midwifery: A systematic review and responsible AI toolkit.
source: PubMed · International journal of nursing studies
desc: [International journal of nursing studies] Artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, models, and tools are increasingly used in healthcare to support clinical decision-making, administrative workflows, and patient care but key ethical concerns such as accountability, equity, and transparency exist which affect nursing and midwifery practice. However, this discourse often overlooks the relational, contextual, and embodied aspects of care. Our systematic review aimed to critically identify, appraise and synthesise the evidence on ethical dimensions of AI in nursing and midwifery to address these complex issues. We undertook a systematic review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses checklist. We conducted a comprehensive search using key AI, ethics, nursing and midwifery terms across CINAHL, Embase, MEDLINE, The Philosopher's Index and PsycINFO in March 2025. We screened results on Covidence against eligibility criteria using independent reviewers and performed quality assessment. We extracted data and applied inductive thematic synthesis to identify key themes. Six themes emerged. First, preserving humanity emphasised care ethics in AI-mediated nursing and midwifery practice. Second, beyond technical reliability explored safety as an ethical and relational imperative examining premature deployment risks, misinformation as patient harm, and risk mitigation. Third, autonomy, authority and accountability focused on governance challenges and solutions including patient and professional autonomy. Fourth, beyond transparency examined privacy threats, trust-building, and the governance roles of nurses and midwives. Fifth, justice in development and deployment concentrated on algorithmic bias and equitable implementation. Sixth, workforce preparation and deployment centred on capacity gaps and training, critical thinking and ethical awareness, academic integrity, and implementation barriers. Our review offers timely and original insights of the ethical dimensions of AI in nursing and midwifery by capturing interconnected tensions between technological innovation and core professional values across relational care, patient safety, governance, information stewardship, equity and justice, and workforce preparedness. Clear recommendations include an urgent need for education to improve AI literacy, robust, inclusive and flexible AI governance, and the implementation of AI tools aligned with nurses and midwives' values and workflows. title: Prompting Strategies for Readability Alignment Between User-Generated Ophthalmology Questions and Large Language Model Answers: Comparative Evaluation Study.
desc: [JMIR formative research] Accessible health communication is essential for effective patient education, yet most medical information remains written at a level above the general population's recommended reading level. Large language models (LLMs) can simplify complex medical information, but it remains unclear whether responses can be automatically adapted to match the linguistic complexity of user-generated questions seeking medical information. To evaluate whether the LLM-generated responses to user-generated ophthalmology questions align with their readability and to compare different prompting strategies for readability control across multiple LLM architectures, including their impact on response quality as well as computational cost and efficiency. A total of 400 user-generated ophthalmology questions collected from public YouTube comments were categorized into 3 readability tiers based on the Flesch Reading Ease Score. A controlled comparative evaluation of responses generated by 4 LLMs (GPT 5.2, Gemini 3, Claude Opus 4.5, and OSS-20b) was performed under 4 prompting conditions: Baseline (no readability control), Formula-Informed Readability Prompt, Semantic Readability Inference, and External Calculator-Guided Prompt. Agreement between question and response readability was assessed using quadratic-weighted Cohen kappa. Response quality was evaluated using BERTScore and LLM-as-a-judge assessments. Computational efficiency was evaluated through token usage, estimated cost per response, and latency. The external calculator-guided strategy produced the strongest alignment in readability across models, achieving the highest agreement (Gemini 3: κ=0.94; GPT 5.2: κ=0.90), while maintaining favorable computational efficiency. Formula-informed prompting showed intermediate performance, whereas semantic inference demonstrated poor agreement due to unreliable readability estimation. High-performing models (GPT 5.2 and Gemini 3) maintained very high factual accuracy (>98%) across strategies, indicating that readability control did not substantially degrade correctness. In contrast, the open-source OSS-20b model showed lower accuracy (83.75%-90%) and greater sensitivity to readability constraints. Semantic similarity remained high across models (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers Score [BERTScore] F1>0.87). title: A paradigm shift toward explainable and federated intelligence for brain tumor MRI analysis.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Deep learning techniques in brain tumor analysis using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans have improved significantly, but their clinical deployment is limited by models with limited interpretability ('black-box' models) and data privacy limitations. This paper analyses recent literature and aims to explore the intersection of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) and Federated Learning (FL). Following the PRISMA protocol, a systematic search was conducted in Scopus on February 24, 2026, covering English-language journal articles and conference proceedings published from January 2020 to February 2026. The search initially identified 767 records, which were screened using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria for MRI-based brain tumor studies addressing deep learning, explainability, privacy, or Federated Learning, resulting in 147 initially retained studies for the final screening set. One study was subsequently identified as formally retracted and excluded from the final synthesis, resulting in 146 included studies. The review classifies the literature into five primary research themes in brain tumor analysis: explainability, deep learning frameworks, privacy-preserving learning, advanced architectures (Transformers and Mamba), and multimodal learning. The literature suggests a paradigm shift in brain tumor analysis toward model interpretability using XAI. However, there is a significant knowledge gap in privacy-preserving collaborative learning models. Advanced architectures are proposed to solve brain tumor problems, but there are still limitations in model generalization, computational costs, and clinical reliability.

title: The surgeon in the loop: automation bias and human-AI interaction in robotic surgery.
desc: [Surgical endoscopy] Artificial intelligence systems for intraoperative surgical guidance are approaching clinical deployment, yet no study has quantified automation bias (defined as the tendency to over-rely on automated recommendations) in the context of surgical decision-making. As these systems enter operative workflows, the surgeon's ability to recognize and override incorrect AI guidance becomes a critical safety requirement. To measure the extent to which surgeons modify incision plans after exposure to AI-labeled visual guidance and to determine the rate at which incorrect AI suggestions are accepted. A two-phase controlled experiment was conducted among 19 surgeons (10 residents, 2 fellows, 7 attendings). Participants drew incision lines on 20 static frames from robotic cholecystectomy videos, first without guidance (Phase 01) and then with a mock AI overlay (Phase 02). Overlays were either correct (derived from expert consensus) or deliberately incorrect (shifted toward unsafe anatomy) at an approximately 70:30 ratio. No actual AI model was used. The primary outcome was mean perpendicular distance (MPD) between Phase 01 and Phase 02 lines. Secondary outcomes included AI-corridor adherence, over-reliance and under-reliance rates, behavioral accuracy, and confidence shift. Across 231 paired observations, MPD did not differ significantly between correct (75.5 pixels; SD, 33.4) and incorrect (71.1 pixels; SD, 31.7) overlay conditions (P = .35). Directional analysis revealed that surgeons accepted incorrect AI suggestions in 60.6% of incorrect-overlay frames (43/71), with a specificity for rejecting incorrect guidance of only 39.4% (28/71). Correct suggestions were accepted 76.9% of the time (123/160). Overall behavioral accuracy was 65.4%. Self-reported confidence increased significantly after AI exposure (Δ = + 0.65; P < .001). Surgeons accepted approximately 3 of every 5 incorrect AI recommendations. As intraoperative AI systems approach deployment, surgeon oversight cannot be assumed to neutralize algorithmic error; it must be empirically measured, deliberately designed for, and prospectively validated.

title: Too good to be true? AI performance in CT-based urinary stone detection and classification: EAU endourology systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
desc: [World journal of urology] To evaluate pooled performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in computed tomography (CT)-based urinary stone detection and classification and identify methodological factors influencing results. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261319940). A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted up to March 15, 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based detection or classification of urolithiasis on CT with available validation/test cohort data (sensitivity/specificity or 2 × 2 tables) were included. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves. Meta-regression explored moderators related to dataset composition and AI pipelines. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-AI. 14 studies (five detection-based, nine classification-based) were included. Overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.967 and 0.979 (AUC 0.987). Classification studies demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity (0.977) and specificity (0.990) compared with detection studies (0.935 and 0.919; AUC 0.945). Significant heterogeneity was observed and influenced by training sample size, class imbalance, presence of bladder stones or other pathologies, and architectural choices. Most studies had high risk of bias, lacked external validation, and frequently used slice-level or pre-selected datasets, potentially overestimating performance. Substantial methodological heterogeneity and high risk of bias limit clinical generalizability. Detection studies better reflect real-world workflows and show lower performance. Current evidence does not support routine clinical implementation without standardized reporting and robust external validation.

title: A Fully Automated Segment-Specific CCTA Plaque Quantification Workflow using Deep Learning.
source: PubMed · Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
desc: [Journal of imaging informatics in medicine] Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) remains essential for diagnosing coronary artery disease, while the focus has moved from stenosis to plaque burden. Current workflows either need manual adjustments that limit consistency and efficiency, or they lack segment-specific precision. This study evaluated the effectiveness and reliability of a fully automated deep learning-based plaque quantification method using CCTA. DVPlaque workflow, a fully automated deep learning model, was developed to quantify segment-specific plaque volume. A total of 271 CCTA scans were included. Plaque quantification was performed by the expert and DVPlaque model, respectively. Reliability was measured through interclass correlation coefficient (ICC) analysis and Bland-Altman plots. DVPlaque workflow cost less time than expert measurement (p 0.90, and per-segment ICCs were > 0.90 except for mid-LAD NCP (0.887). DVPlaque scheme was capable of quantifying plaque volume with excellent efficiency. The automated quantification of CP and NCP exhibited strong reliability even on a per-segment level, facilitating clinical application.

title: A Lightweight EEG-Based Alzheimer's Disease Detection Framework on an Edge-Computing Platform Toward Future Intelligent Digital Twin Systems.
desc: [Journal of integrative neuroscience] Alzheimer's disease (AD) progresses slowly through several stages until the patient reaches full cognitive decline. The electroencephalography (EEG) alterations associated with AD often emerge before symptom onset, suggesting that accessible and repeated EEG-based assessment could facilitate earlier detection and longitudinal monitoring. However, this type of assessment requires an AD detection model operating on edge-computing platforms within the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT). At present, many existing AD detection models rely on complex deep learning architectures with numerous parameters, which significantly limit their practicality for on-edge deployment. We propose an on-edge AD detection framework comprising a lightweight dilated hybrid deep learning (DHDL) model with a channel selection approach to reduce the computational and power demands on the evaluated edge-computing platform. A key architectural component is the inclusion of dual-granularity dilated temporal convolutions. This method expands the receptive field at two scales to capture both short- and long-term temporal features from EEG signals without increasing the number of parameters. Subsequently, several hybrid lightweight layers extract distinct temporal and spatial features and are integrated with attention mechanisms. Additionally, our channel selection approach first forms an initial subset of EEG channels guided by individual channel classification accuracy, and then iteratively refines the selected channels using hill-climbing optimization. Here, we evaluated our framework on two publicly available EEG datasets recorded for the same group of subjects (n = 48 subjects): a conventional closed-eye (CE) dataset and a more challenging open-eye (OE) dataset. Validation followed a subject-independent Leave-2-Subjects-Out (L2SO) cross-validation protocol. Real-time deployment was tested on an edge-computing platform. The proposed framework achieved 92.56% accuracy for the CE dataset and 75.15% accuracy for the OE dataset. Inference required 10.45 ms and 8.23 ms per segment for the CE and OE datasets, respectively, and consumed 9.69 mJ and 6.95 mJ of energy per segment, respectively. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework as a real-time, on-edge inference module for AD detection. Although a complete intelligent digital twin system is not implemented in this work, the proposed framework can serve as an inference component for future digital twin systems, su

title: Evaluation of large language models for guideline-based clinical questions in muscle-invasive and non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer and upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multidisciplinary Delphi study.
source: PubMed · Journal of comparative effectiveness research
desc: [Journal of comparative effectiveness research] Aim: To assess expert panel agreement with responses from three large language models, Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT, to questions based on guidelines for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). Materials & methods: The 2025 European Association of Urology (EAU) guidelines were provided to Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-4.1-mini. Figures and tables were converted into plain language text. Each model answered 25 questions per entity. Panels of 7-10 experts rated responses on a 9-point scale using a modified Delphi process with two rounds. Outcomes were consensus in agreement and median expert panel score ≥7. Results: For Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT, respectively, consensus in agreement was achieved for 88%, 100% and 96% of NMIBC responses (p = 0.097); 92%, 100% and 96% of MIBC responses (p = 0.223); and 56%, 100% and 96% of UTUC responses (p < 0.001). For UTUC, significantly fewer Claude responses achieved consensus in agreement than Gemini or ChatGPT responses. Across all questions, consensus in agreement was achieved for 59/75 Claude responses (78.7%), 75/75 Gemini responses (100%), and 72/75 ChatGPT responses (96%) (p < 0.001). Median scores ≥7 were achieved for 88%, 100% and 100% of NMIBC responses; 96%, 100% and 100% of MIBC responses; and 68%, 100% and 96% of UTUC responses. In UTUC, Claude had significantly fewer such responses than Gemini, but the difference from ChatGPT was not statistically significant. Overall, median scores ≥7 were achieved for 63/75 Claude responses (84%), 75/75 Gemini responses (100%) and 74/75 ChatGPT responses (98.7%) (p < 0.001). Conclusion: Under the study conditions, large language model responses frequently achieved expert panel agreement, particularly for Gemini and ChatGPT, supporting the potential of these models for guideline interpretation. Further validation is required to establish clinical utility and safety.

title: Engineering Neural Interface Materials for Brain-Computer Interfaces: Toward Reliable Neural Information and Functional Recovery.
desc: [Biomaterials research] Motor dysfunction is a major disabling outcome of neurological disorders, including stroke, spinal cord injury, and cerebral palsy. By establishing direct communication between neural activity and external effectors, brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising strategy for neural functional reconstruction, enabling motor intention decoding, assistive control, and rehabilitation feedback. However, sustained BCI performance depends not only on advances in decoding algorithms but also on neural interface materials and interfacial properties, as well as the reliable transfer of neural information across signal acquisition, intelligent decoding, control execution, and closed-loop feedback. Existing reviews have mainly focused on invasiveness, electrode technologies, or decoding methods, with comparatively limited integration of neural interface materials, signal reliability, artificial intelligence (AI) adaptability, and closed-loop performance within a unified information reliability framework. Therefore, this review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled BCIs for motor rehabilitation, compares neural signal and interface characteristics across different levels of invasiveness, examines the effects of key material and interfacial properties on stable signal acquisition, and discusses the roles of AI in data-efficient learning, spatiotemporal and relational neural representation, adaptation to neural distribution shifts, and efficient decoding for real-time closed-loop operation. Representative applications in exoskeletons, neuroprostheses, cerebral palsy rehabilitation, and rehabilitation robotics are further summarized. Finally, current challenges and potential solutions spanning neural interface stability to functional recovery are discussed, providing a systematic pathway toward long-term reliable BCIs and the clinical translation of next-generation intelligent neurorehabilitation systems.

title: Deep learning denoising and positron range correction of clinical [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TOC PET images.
desc: [Zeitschrift fur medizinische Physik] PET image quality degradation due to positron range effects in high-energy positron-emitting radionuclides such as Gallium-68 (68Ga) can be mitigated by applying positron range correction (PRC). Deep learning (DL) models have been shown to improve image quality by reducing image noise. This study aimed to evaluate a DL model for simultaneous denoising and 68Ga-specific PRC in clinical [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TOC PET scans. Three different U-Net-based DL models were trained to map reduced-count PET images reconstructed without PRC (25%, 33%, or 50% of acquired counts) to full-count PET images reconstructed with tissue-independent PRC (FC-PRC). The generated reduced-count-enhanced images (RCE-25%, RCE-33%, RCE-50%) were evaluated using the mean standardized uptake value (SUVmean) in liver and lung, noise levels in liver, and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) of soft tissue lesions. Three experienced nuclear medicine physicians assessed the overall image quality (OIQ), overall diagnostic confidence (ODC), and lesion detectability (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy). Compared to FC-PRC, RCE-33% and RCE-50% exhibited similar noise, whereas RCE-25% showed substantial residual noise. CNR was reduced for RCE-33% (-5.6%, p=0.001) and RCE-25% (-8.0%, p 90%). The proposed DL-based approach achieved comparable noise and image quality down to 50% of counts. Although it did not outperform the reconstruction-based PRC, its benefit lies in simultaneous denoising and PRC in a single step.

title: Plant Single-Cell Metabolomics and Metabolite Imaging: Current Advances and Future Directions.
desc: [The Plant cell] Plants are multicellular systems composed of highly specialized cell types, whose distinct transcriptomes, proteomes, and metabolomes collectively shape growth, development, defense, and environmental adaptation. While single-cell transcriptomics has transformed our understanding of plant cellular heterogeneity, metabolites provide a direct and integrative readout of cellular biochemical activity and physiological state and can offer valuable insights into phenotype. They provide essential information that gene expression alone does not capture. Recent advances in mass spectrometry-based single-cell metabolomics (scMet) have enabled direct measurement of metabolic variation across individual cells and subcellular domains. In parallel, mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) has emerged as a powerful approach for mapping the spatial organization of metabolites within intact plant organs, offering new opportunities to connect chemical diversity with anatomy, cell identity, and biological functions. This review summarizes current technologies for plant single-cell sampling, scMet, and MSI for spatial metabolomics. It further highlights emerging efforts to illuminate the plant's cellular and spatial dark metabolome through spectral libraries, computational metabolomics, and AI-assisted annotation. A long-term objective is to build quantitative, spatially resolved, and biologically interpretable plant signaling and metabolic networks at single-cell resolution.

title: Limited capital? Explaining transatlantic divergences in artificial intelligence startup financing.
desc: [PloS one] Artificial intelligence (AI) is a global general-purpose technology (GPT), yet the financial systems that scale AI ventures differ markedly across regions. This paper compares AI-focused venture capital (VC) dynamics in Europe and the United States from 2000 to 2025 using approximately 8,000 AI-related VC rounds from PitchBook and macroeconomic and institutional data from the World Bank. Exploiting the 2021 generative-AI inflection point as a common technological shock that triggered a structural reallocation of venture capital toward AI ventures, we apply a difference-in-differences (DiD) design to distinguish between startup formation and scale-up financing. Descriptive evidence shows that Europe keeps pace with the US in AI deal counts, suggesting no major pipeline gap in startup formation. However, Europe lags substantially in AI investment volumes and in AI's share of total VC funding. In the Post-period, AI accounts for around 60% of VC investment volume in the US, compared to roughly 31% in Europe. Difference-in-differences estimates are consistent with parallel trajectories in AI deal activity but point to large and statistically significant transatlantic gaps in AI investment volume and investment intensity. These results are robust to macroeconomic and governance controls, a formal event-study test of pre-treatment trends, and a sensitivity analysis that excludes the United Kingdom (which alone accounts for roughly 31% of European VC volume), a placebo test using a false treatment year, and the exclusion of the COVID-19 period. Interpreting the findings through GPT diffusion and the Varieties of Capitalism framework, we interpret the pattern as being consistent with the US liberal market economy having a structural advantage in mobilizing large-scale risk capital. The results inform current debates on European technological sovereignty, the Capital Markets Union, and AI-related policy initiatives.

title: EEG-based deep learning estimates preterm infants' cerebral age: Contribution of slow-wave and cross-frequency coupling.
desc: [iScience] Reliably estimating cerebral maturation in preterm newborns is crucial for early identification of atypical neurodevelopment. We developed a deep-learning framework using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict postmenstrual age (PMA) from spontaneous neural activity in EEG recordings of 165 healthy preterm infants (28-38 weeks PMA). The model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.75 ± 0.60 weeks, with 73.9% of prediction errors within one week. To identify key neurophysiological drivers, we systematically manipulated signal components. Results showed that removing low-frequency activity ( 12 Hz) had minimal impact. Our results demonstrate that maturation signatures are primarily driven by slow-wave dynamics and their hierarchical coupling with faster oscillations, which are fundamental hallmarks of early neurodevelopment.

title: Learning Constraints in Protein Evolution beyond Known Substitution Frequencies.
desc: [Molecular biology and evolution] During the evolution of protein sequences, amino acid substitutions follow broad patterns that are well established, such as those induced by the physico-chemical properties of residues or the position of sites along the sequence. While these deviations from random changes have been exploited for practical applications, such as to simulate protein evolution or to score protein alignments, they are too general to predict the precise evolution of individual protein sequences. To investigate whether protein sequences contain contextual information about their subsequent evolution beyond that captured by conventional substitution statistics and evolutionary conservation, we trained deep learning models based on an Evolutionary Scale Modelling (ESM2) encoder to predict the rate, the position and the nature of the amino-acid substitutions in the evolution of ancestral sequences and compared their performance to simpler and explainable heuristics. Our results show that predicting the rate of amino acid changes is achieved equally well by deep learning and by using evolutionary information in outgroup sequences. This suggests that the protein sequence does not contain information that significantly improves the predictions for this task. On the opposite, we show that deep learning models predict the position of these substitutions more accurately than statistics-based baselines. Predictions of the nature of substitutions largely outperform baselines, with over 37% accuracy overall. We observe that rapidly evolving sequences are harder to predict and substitutions preferentially occur between chemically similar amino acids. Interestingly, predictive information is predominantly contained within a local sequence context of 16 residues. These findings indicate that the nature of substitutions in protein evolution is partly governed by predictive rules that remain to be discovered through a more accurate modelling that could describe evolutionary trajectories based on sequence context alone.

title: Crack identification and detection in mine boreholes using deep learning: A case study of hexi coal mine.
desc: [PloS one] The internal cracks in deep rock masses are an important factor determining the safety of coal mining. The borehole peeping technology is an important method for obtaining the distribution of coal and rock fractures in deep geological engineering. However, there are often problems such as strong background interference and complex joints in real mines, which bring greater challenges to obtaining the distribution of cracks. Therefore, this study proposes a deep learning-based method for identifying internal cracks, which is used for the intelligent identification and analysis of cracks in drilled rock masses. The experimental verification was carried out based on the real borehole peeping images of the tunnels in Hexi Coal Mine as the data set. By embedding the ResCBAM attention mechanism into the YOLOv8 head network, the reliability and accuracy of identifying internal cracks in rock were further enhanced. The test results show that, the proposed Res-YOLOv8 algorithm can more accurately suppress the interference of complex backgrounds and present the morphological characteristics of rock cracks to compare with the fusion of typical attention mechanisms SE and CBAM with YOLOv8. The ResCBAM-YOLOv8 algorithm demonstrates strong performance in the evaluation indicators of confusion matrix, loss rate, precision, recall and MPA. The proposal of method has improved the efficiency of detecting and identifying cracks in coal and rock masses in real mines, and provided more reliable technical support for the stability evaluation of coal mine roof.

title: Deep-Learning-Driven Dual Sensors Based on Single-Trapped Upconverting Particles.
desc: [Nano letters] Upconverting lanthanide-doped particles are widely used as nanoscale temperature sensors, particularly in biological and photonic environments. However, extending their functionality to simultaneously measure temperature and light intensity remains a challenge, as the luminescent response is highly sensitive to both the environment composition and its temperature. In this work, we combine deep-learning methods with large-scale spectral data sets to investigate the reliability of Er/Yb-doped particles to function as dual sensors. Spectral data are collected from single particles levitating in vacuum and ensembles of particles in application-relevant wet and dry media. Although traditional ratiometric methods reliably retrieve temperature irrespective of the environment and specific experimental apparatus, they fail to disentangle the complex dependencies needed for dual sensing. Our trained models overcome these limitations, accurately predicting both temperature and laser power despite environmental variability. This approach opens a new route toward robust, data-driven sensing with upconverting particles in complex or fluctuating conditions.
